sections.h2: Where is Lakewood, Colorado, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Lakewood is the most populous city in Jefferson County and the fifth most populous in Colorado, sitting immediately west of Denver. It had 155,984 residents at the 2020 census.

The city covers about 44.6 square miles at an elevation of 5,656 feet, on the western edge of the Great Plains just east of the Front Range. Green Mountain, at 6,854 feet, rises in the far west-central part of the city. Lakewood borders Wheat Ridge to the north, Edgewater to the northeast, Denver to the east and southeast, Morrison to the southwest and Golden to the northwest.

A city this size is really several markets. A house near Belmar, one near Green Mountain and one along West Colfax can have little in common beyond a city name, so a good offer starts with the specific address.

Lakewood began in 1889 when Charles Welch and W.A.H. Loveland platted a 13-block area along Colfax Avenue west of Denver. It stayed an unincorporated community for eight decades and became a city on June 24, 1969, at first under the name Jefferson City. Voters soon changed it to Lakewood.

The city never had a traditional downtown. West Colfax Avenue, once US 40, served as the main route from Denver into the mountains and filled with shops, motels and restaurants by the 1950s. Later, the Villa Italia Mall on West Alameda declined and was replaced by Belmar, which now serves as the city's town center.

Before incorporation, Lakewood relied on separate water districts, fire districts and Jefferson County government, and some neighborhoods lacked street lights and sidewalks. A buyer of an older Lakewood house may ask about street lighting, sidewalks and utilities, since those were handled neighborhood by neighborhood in the early years.

Government is the largest employment group in Lakewood, led by the Denver Federal Center. The city's 2023 annual report lists the top ten employers below.

A job tied to a federal or state agency can mean a transfer order with a firm report date. A seller on that clock usually cares most about certainty of closing.

sections.h2: How do roads and rail connect Lakewood?
sections.html:
Nine highways pass through Lakewood, and a light rail line serves seven stations inside the city.

  • Interstate 70 enters from Applewood to the east and exits to West Pleasant View in the west.
  • US 6 (6th Avenue Freeway), US 40 (West Colfax) and US 285 carry east-west and southern traffic.
  • State Highways 8, 95, 121, 391 and 470 round out the network, with Highway 121 running along South Wadsworth Boulevard.
  • The Regional Transportation District opened W Line light rail service on April 26, 2013.
  • Bustang's West Line stops at Federal Center station on the way to Grand Junction.

Whether a house sits near a W Line station is one of many details we look at when we review a property.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges are in Lakewood?
sections.html:
Lakewood is part of Jefferson County School District R-1, and the city also hosts four higher-education institutions. High schools inside the city include Lakewood, Green Mountain, Bear Creek, Brady Exploration and Alameda International, and the private Colorado Academy is also located here.

Colorado Christian University, Red Rocks Community College, Rocky Mountain College of Art and Design and the Colorado School of Trades are all in Lakewood.

sections.h2: What is the Lakewood climate and landscape like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Lakewood has a cold semi-arid climate. Several small creeks and gulches cross the city and drain east toward the South Platte River, including Lakewood Gulch, Weir Gulch, Sanderson Gulch and Bear Creek.

Lakes and reservoirs also dot the city, among them Bear Creek Lake, Kendrick Lake, Cottonwood Lake and the Soda Lakes. If your property sits next to a gulch or reservoir, a buyer's inspector may look closely at grading and basement moisture.

  • Note any past water in a basement or crawl space and what was done about it.
  • Keep records of gutter, grading or sump work.
  • Tell a buyer about known issues up front instead of leaving them for the inspection.

sections.h2: What licensing rules might a Lakewood landlord face?
sections.html:
Lakewood requires a license to operate a short-term rental, and the City Clerk's Office handles applications. The city began taking online applications for new short-term rental licenses on May 1, 2023, and incomplete applications are not accepted.

The clerk's office is at 480 S. Allison Parkway, and the licensing contact is STR@lakewoodco.gov or 303-987-7080. The city also runs an online complaint form for reports of unlicensed rentals. You can read the process on the Lakewood short-term rental license page.

If you own a house you rented short term and want out, a cash sale lets you skip finding a buyer who wants the license.

sections.h2: When are Jefferson County property taxes due for a Lakewood house?
sections.html:
Lakewood homeowners pay property tax to the Jefferson County Treasurer in Golden, and Colorado taxes are collected in arrears. The county's page lists its 2026 deadlines below.

Payment2026 due date (Jefferson County)
First installmentMarch 2 (the county was closed on Saturday, February 28)
Second installmentJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Notices go out by the end of January, and this is the only notice the county sends. Delinquent notices follow in July, and a tax lien sale takes place each November for unpaid real property. If a due date lands on a Friday or weekend, the county accepts payment the next business day without interest.

The Treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway, Suite 2520, and it is open Monday through Thursday and closed on Fridays. More is on the Jefferson County Important Dates page.

sections.h2: What places and parks define Lakewood?
sections.html:
Lakewood has several landmarks that give buyers a sense of place. Belmar is the town center, mixing retail, residential, cultural and public space, and the Lakewood Cultural Center houses a theater, gallery space and art classrooms.

Heritage Lakewood Belmar Park is a museum and festival grounds with historic buildings near Kountze Lake, and the 40 West Arts District runs a bike and walking art experience along the light rail line. Lakewood was named an All-America City for the first time in 2011.

These amenities are part of what draws people to the city, and they are part of what you can mention when a buyer asks about the neighborhood.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale look like in Lakewood?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Lakewood skips the lender, so closing depends on title work and your preferred date. We buy as-is, which means you leave out the repairs and staging that a listing normally demands.

That fits several common Lakewood situations: an inherited house, a house with tenants, a rental you want to exit before licensing becomes a burden, or a house where a move date is fixed. Send us the address and your timeline, and we will respond with an offer or an honest explanation.

faqs.q: What county is Lakewood, CO in?
faqs.a: Lakewood is in Jefferson County, where it is the most populous city. Property tax goes to the Jefferson County Treasurer in Golden.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Lakewood?
faqs.a: Jefferson County's 2026 schedule lists March 2 and June 15 for two installments, or April 30 for one full payment. Taxes are collected in arrears, so the bill covers the previous year.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lakewood?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 155,984 residents, which made Lakewood the fifth most populous city in Colorado.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Lakewood house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Lakewood has a short-term rental license handled by the City Clerk's Office, and it began taking online applications on May 1, 2023. Check the current ordinance for the full requirements.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lakewood house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses in their present condition, so you do not need to repair or clean the property before closing.
